coverage.category: 31. Business licence holders in reserved sectors (Business Licensing and Registration Act 2019 and Regulations; Regulation 34 and Schedule 16)
coverage.found: Act and Regulations in force from 1 Aug 2022. Regulation 34 reserves activities for indigenous citizens (logistics, clearing, warehousing, business agents and brokers, cleaning, printing and photocopying, installation trades, scrap metal, pharmacy retail, fuel and LPG retail). Reported plan to stop issuing or renewing licences for any enterprise with a non-indigenous owner or director from Jan 2026; the law-firm article dated 30 Mar 2026 gives info as at 3 Dec 2025, so enforcement is unverified. A rule change, but advisory rather than software. See C03.

coverage.category: 32. Medicinal cannabis licensees (Drugs of Abuse (Cannabis) Regulations 2018)
coverage.found: Licences run 12 months and must be renewed yearly. Minister declared in July 2025 that licences not reported to the ministry or not renewed within 12 months are cancelled. Licensees must show security, cultivation, processing and financial reporting. Fees M150,000 (grow only) to M500,000, renewal M350,000 (older figures). Corruption allegations. Few, well-funded buyers. See C04.

coverage.category: 35. Data protection (Data Protection Act 2011/2012)
coverage.found: The Data Protection Commission has not been established (April and September 2026 sources), so there is no registration process or deadline.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water Act 2008 (Act 15 of 2008) s.20 requires a water use permit (Form A, fee, valid 5 years, Director supervises), s.21 a construction permit for waterworks (5 years), and s.22 requires anyone drilling boreholes or digging wells to register with the Director and receive a drilling contractor's certificate (Form C); the Director keeps a public register of boreholes and wells. Read from the Act PDF (ampeid.org copy, text extracted locally); lesotholii.org returned 403. No public online register or filing portal found, no driller count, and no regulations found beyond the Act. Ministry paid drillers M18,000-25,000 per borehole in 2020, private drillers charged about M40,000 (The Reporter, 2020). Likely a few dozen drillers; permit holders are mostly farms, lodges, schools, mines and NGOs. Thin buyer base for software; see candidate C1.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: No Lesotho licensing regime found for septic exhausters or waste haulers. UN-Habitat 2022 profile says there is no national municipal solid waste law (Environment Act 2008, Local Government Act, Public Health Order 1970 apply). Ombudsman report (The Reporter, 2026) says about 137,510 t/yr waste and only 20 percent is formally collected. Maseru sewerage serves few customers; most use pit latrines. Effluent discharge permits exist under Water Act s.27 but apply to dischargers, not haulers. Nothing new beyond the absence of a duty; no candidate.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Could not confirm any boiler, lift or pressure-vessel register or certificate in Lesotho. WageIndicator (updated March 2026) says the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2024 (enacted April 2024 with the Labour Act 2024, per ILO) requires an annual workplace safety and health audit by a competent person, the report to be kept for inspectors, and employers with 50+ workers to appoint a registered safety practitioner. The older Factories, Machinery and Equipment Safety Regulations 1984 are the likely home of boiler rules; their current status is unverified. ILO says workplace registration for inspection is incomplete and inspections lag. Candidate C2 (annual audit) is the only lead; I could not read the Act text.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Rural supply runs through village water committees (VWCs) under the rural water department; a NUL case study finds VWC bye-laws lack legal force, tenure is open-ended, members are unpaid and untrained. LEWA regulates urban water licences and tariffs (LEWA licence fee and complaints regulations 2013); its 2013 urban quality standards exclude rural supply. A Water and Sanitation Services Bill was mentioned as proposed; passage unconfirmed. No mandatory filing duty found for small schemes. Weak lead C3 (fee ledger for VWCs).

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Societies registered with the Registrar General's Office (Ministry of Justice and Law) under the Societies Act as amended 2001: constitution plus annual fee to keep registration valid; sources describe a paper process, with no online list of registered societies. No 2024-2025 NGO Act or Societies Bill found; a draft NGO policy would create a register and annual reports but its status is unconfirmed. Lesotho Council of NGOs is a voluntary body, not a registrar. Annual fee tracking alone is too thin; weak candidate C4. Halal and kosher not relevant.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: gov.ls e-service page lists a Contractors Registration Certificate (requires application letter, traders licence, tax clearance certificate, equipment registrations; categories A-D with figures 2000/1500/500/300, currency not stated; 3-month processing; issuer, renewal and validity not stated). No Lesotho construction council act found. Local-content: 2018 directive reported by Lesotho Times that tenders up to M10m go to majority Basotho-owned firms; Lowlands Water Project Phase II and LHDA Phase II have 30 percent local subcontract commitments; enforcement reported weak (Reporter and Tribune, 2026). Mines and Minerals Act 2005 and Amendment 2021/22 legalised small-scale diamond mining by Basotho: permit for up to 100 m2, operations must start within 2 months, registration through chiefs and local councils. No quarry register found; the dissertation 'History of aggregate mining in Lesotho 1967-2022' at repository.tml.nul.ls is unread. Candidates C5, C6, C7, all weak.

result.reason: The duty looks real. The Tourism Levy Act 2006 was operational from 1 Oct 2022 and operators must register with LTDC. Accommodation providers charge the levy per night, reported at 1.5% of room rate (some 2022 reports said 5%). Contraventions carry a fine up to M10,000, up to 6 months in jail, or both. I found no official portal or software for levy collection, but I ran only two searches. Return format and filing frequency were not found. The market is tiny: 129 registered at first, then 272 in 2024, and total collections were only about M4m. Low willingness to pay and a small buyer pool keep the score at 3.

Duty is real: Drugs of Abuse (Cannabis) Regulations 2018 (LN 40 of 2018) include seed-to-sale tracking and record keeping. The July 2025 minister's notice (Drugs of Abuse Act 2008 s.23) says licences are cancelled if unreported or not renewed within 12 months. No Lesotho-specific vendor or state portal was found, though I did not search deeply. The market is tiny: roughly 140-145 licences were issued by 2019, only about 5-8 operating, and the current count is unknown. Buyers are few, licensing is politically entangled, and the real regulatory reporting content is unverified. Renewal fees of about M370k imply the operators have money, but a solo founder has almost no addressable market. Weak candidate.

The duty is plausible but rests only on a secondary source. WageIndicator (page updated March 2026) says the OSH Act 2024 requires a workplace safety and health audit at least every 12 months by a competent person. The report must be kept for inspectors, and workplaces with 50 or more workers must appoint a registered practitioner. The page gives no penalty amounts. I did not find the Act text, a definition of competent person, or commencement or regulations status. No Lesotho OSH audit software or auditor register turned up, but the search was thin. Enforcement is reportedly weak (the claim cites an ILO project on lagging inspections) and the market is tiny. I found no employer count. Willingness to pay is doubtful. I did not run a Sesotho search. The claim's "boilers and lifts" category is not supported by the sources I found.
